# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

Notes

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is

      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)

- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

<output>
# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
> If you know a solution, please tell me.

## Random Notes
- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
  that lesson; no need to stress.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.

            # if len>1 because prev missed earlier? print
            if len(new)==0:
                # failed to discover
                break
            else:
                # try to continue? Ambiguity fatal; break
                ordered.extend(sorted(new)); prev=cur; continue
        ordered.append(next(iter(new)))
        prev=cur
        if top%10==0:
            print("SO_FAR", ordered, flush=True)
    print("FINAL", mode, ordered)
    return ordered

        let mut fg = Color::Reset;
        let mut bg = Color::Reset;
        #[cfg(feature = "underline-color")]
        let mut underline_color = Color::Reset;
        let mut modifier = Modifier::empty();
        let mut last_pos: Option<Position> = None;
        for (x, y, cell) in content {
            // Move the cursor if the previous location was not (x - 1, y)
            if !matches!(last_pos, Some(p) if x == p.x + 1 && y == p.y) {
                queue!(self.writer, MoveTo(x, y))?;
            }
            last_pos = Some(Position { x, y });
            if cell.modifier != modifier {
                let diff = ModifierDiff {
                    from: modifier,
                    to: cell.modifier,
                };
                diff.queue(&mut self.writer)?;
                modifier = cell.modifier;
            }
            if cell.fg != fg || cell.bg != bg {
                queue!(

                fg = cell.fg;
                bg = cell.bg;
            }

            if cell.underline_color != underline_color {
                let color = cell.underline_color.into_crossterm();
                queue!(self.writer, SetUnderlineColor(color))?;
                underline_color = cell.underline_color;
            }

            queue!(self.writer, Print(cell.symbol()))?;
        }

            SetBackgroundColor(CrosstermColor::Reset),

// converts KeyCode to KeyEvent (adds shift modifier in case of uppercase characters)
fn char_code_to_event(code: KeyCode) -> KeyEvent {
    let modifiers = match code {
        KeyCode::Char(c) if c.is_uppercase() => KeyModifiers::SHIFT,
        _ => KeyModifiers::empty(),
    };
    KeyEvent::new(code, modifiers)
}

pub(crate) fn parse_csi(buffer: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Option<InternalEvent>> {
    assert!(buffer.starts_with(b"\x1B[")); // ESC [

    if buffer.len() == 2 {
        return Ok(None);
    }

    let input_event = match buffer[2] {
        b'[' => {
            if buffer.len() == 3 {
                None
            } else {
                match buffer[3] {
                    // NOTE (@imdaveho): cannot find when this occurs;
                    // having another '[' after ESC[ not a likely scenario
                    val @ b'A'..=b'E' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::F(1 + val - b'A').into())),
                    _ => return Err(could_not_parse_event_error()),
                }
            }
        }
        b'D' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::Left.into())),
        b'C' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::Right.into())),
        b'A' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::Up.into())),
        b'B' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::Down.into())),
        b'H' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::Home.into())),
        b'F' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::End.into())),
        b'Z' => Some(Event::Key(KeyEvent::new_with_kind(
            KeyCode::BackTab,
            KeyModifiers::SHIFT,
            KeyEventKind::Press,
        ))),
        b'M' => return parse_csi_normal_mouse(buffer),
        b'<' => return parse_csi_sgr_mouse(buffer),
        b'I' => Some(Event::FocusGained),
        b'O' => Some(Event::FocusLost),
        b';' => return parse_csi_modifier_key_code(buffer),
        // P, Q, and S for compatibility with Kitty keyboard protocol,
        // as the 1 in 'CSI 1 P' etc. must be omitted if there are no
        // modifiers pressed:
        // https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/#legacy-functional-keys
        b'P' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::F(1).into())),
        b'Q' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::F(2).into())),
        b'S' => Some(Event::Key(KeyCode::F(4).into())),
        b'?' => match buffer[buffer.len() - 1] {
            b'u' => return parse_csi_keyboard_enhancement_flags(buffer),
            b'c' => return parse_csi_primary_device_attributes(buffer),
            _ => None,
        },
        b'0'..=b'9' => {
            // Numbered escape code.
            if buffer.len() == 3 {
                None
            } else {
                // The final byte of a CSI sequence can be in the range 64-126, so
                // let's keep reading anything else.
                let last_byte = buffer[buffer.len() - 1];
                if !(64..=126).contains(&last_byte) {
                    None
                } else {
                    #[cfg(feature = "bracketed-paste")]
                    if buffer.starts_with(b"\x1B[200~") {
                        return parse_csi_bracketed_paste(buffer);
                    }
                    match last_byte {
                        b'M' => return parse_csi_rxvt_mouse(buffer),
                        b'~' => return parse_csi_special_key_code(buffer),
                        b'u' => return parse_csi_u_encoded_key_code(buffer),
                        b'R' => return parse_csi_cursor_position(buffer),
                        _ => return parse_csi_modifier_key_code(buffer),
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        _ => return Err(could_not_parse_event_error()),
    };

    Ok(input_event.map(InternalEvent::Event))
}

where
    T: std::str::FromStr,
{
    iter.next()

pub fn parse_layout(name: &str) -> Layout {
    match name {
        "qwertz" => QWERTZ,
        "azerty" => AZERTY,
        "dvorak" => DVORAK,
        "colemak" => COLEMAK,
        "colemakdh" => Layout { rows: ["qwfp", "arstgmneio'", "zxcdvkh,./"], number_row: "`1234567890-=" },
        // "qwerty" and everything else falls back to qwerty
        _ => QWERTY,
    }
}

fn full_string(l: &Layout) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    s.push_str(l.number_row);
    for r in l.rows { s.push_str(r); }
    s

use rand::seq::SliceRandom;
use std::time::Instant;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Opts {
    pub top: i64,
    pub combi: usize,
    pub rep: usize,
    pub wpm: i64,
    pub acc: i64,
}

pub struct Game {
    pub opts: Opts,
    pub ngrams: Vec<String>,
    pub lesson_num: usize,
    pub successes: usize,
    pub fails: usize,
    pub cur_lesson: String,
    pub ngram_count: usize,
    pub time_started: Instant,
    pub has_started: bool,
    pub cumulative_wpm: i64,
    pub cumulative_acc: i64,
    pub last_wpm: i64,
    pub last_acc: i64,
    pub total_keys: i64,
    pub wrong: i64,
    pub input: Vec<char>,
}

impl Game {
    pub fn new(opts: Opts, ngrams: Vec<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            opts,
            ngrams,
            lesson_num: 0,
            successes: 0,
            fails: 0,
            cur_lesson: String::new(),
            ngram_count: 0,
            time_started: Instant::now(),
            has_started: false,
            cumulative_wpm: 0,
            cumulative_acc: 0,
            last_wpm: 0,
            last_acc: 0,
            total_keys: 0,
            wrong: 0,
            input: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn next_lesson(&mut self) {
        let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
        let mut chosen: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..self.opts.combi {
            let c = self.ngrams.choose(&mut rng).unwrap().clone();
            chosen.push(c);
        }
        let mut lesson = String::new();
        for _ in 0..self.opts.rep {
            for c in &chosen {
                lesson.push_str(c);
                lesson.push(' ');
            }
        }
        self.cur_lesson = lesson;
        self.ngram_count = self.opts.combi * self.opts.rep;
        self.lesson_num += 1;
        self.input.clear();
        self.total_keys = 0;
        self.wrong = 0;
        self.has_started = false;
    }

    pub fn avg_wpm(&self) -> i64 {
        let lessons_done = (self.successes + self.fails) as i64;
        if lessons_done == 0 { 0 } else { self.cumulative_wpm / lessons_done }
    }
    pub fn avg_acc(&self) -> i64 {
        let lessons_done = (self.successes + self.fails) as i64;
        if lessons_done == 0 { 0 } else { self.cumulative_acc / lessons_done }
    }

    pub fn check_lesson_completed(&mut self) {
        let input_str: String = self.input.iter().collect();
        if input_str == self.cur_lesson {
            let elapsed = self.time_started.elapsed();
            let non_space = self.cur_lesson.chars().filter(|&c| c != ' ').count() as f64;
            let words = non_space / 5.0;
            let minutes = elapsed.as_secs_f64() / 60.0;
            let wpm = if minutes > 0.0 { (words / minutes) as i64 } else { 0 };
            let acc = if self.total_keys > 0 {
                ((self.total_keys - self.wrong) * 100 / self.total_keys) as i64
            } else { 0 };
            self.last_wpm = wpm;
            self.last_acc = acc;
            if wpm >= self.opts.wpm && acc >= self.opts.acc {
                self.successes += 1;
            } else {
                self.fails += 1;
            }
            self.cumulative_wpm += wpm;
            self.cumulative_acc += acc;
            self.next_lesson();
        }
    }
}

    /// Converts the ratatui type to a crossterm type.
    fn into_crossterm(self) -> C;

struct ModifierDiff {
    pub from: Modifier,
    pub to: Modifier,
}

impl ModifierDiff {
    fn queue<W>(self, mut w: W) -> io::Result<()>
    where
        W: io::Write,
    {
        let removed = self.from - self.to;
        if removed.contains(Modifier::REVERSED) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::NoReverse))?;
        }

        let reset_intensity = removed.contains(Modifier::BOLD) || removed.contains(Modifier::DIM);
        if reset_intensity {
            // Bold and Dim are both reset by applying the Normal intensity
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::NormalIntensity))?;

            // The remaining Bold and Dim attributes must be
            // reapplied after the intensity reset above.
            if self.to.contains(Modifier::DIM) {
                queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Dim))?;
            }

            if self.to.contains(Modifier::BOLD) {
                queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Bold))?;
            }
        }

        if removed.contains(Modifier::ITALIC) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::NoItalic))?;
        }
        if removed.contains(Modifier::UNDERLINED) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::NoUnderline))?;
        }
        if removed.contains(Modifier::CROSSED_OUT) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::NotCrossedOut))?;
        }
        if removed.contains(Modifier::HIDDEN) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::NoHidden))?;
        }
        if removed.contains(Modifier::SLOW_BLINK) || removed.contains(Modifier::RAPID_BLINK) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::NoBlink))?;
        }

        let added = self.to - self.from;
        if added.contains(Modifier::REVERSED) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Reverse))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::BOLD) && !reset_intensity {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Bold))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::ITALIC) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Italic))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::UNDERLINED) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Underlined))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::DIM) && !reset_intensity {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Dim))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::CROSSED_OUT) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::CrossedOut))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::HIDDEN) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::Hidden))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::SLOW_BLINK) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::SlowBlink))?;
        }
        if added.contains(Modifier::RAPID_BLINK) {
            queue!(w, SetAttribute(CrosstermAttribute::RapidBlink))?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

{"command":"# No clap_derive crate in cache (so original derive not available offline - builder API it is).
# Could intercept clap errors: use try_get_matches() instead of get_matches(), and when error is UnknownArgument with a suggested arg, reformat the usage line to the alternation form before printing/exit. Clap Error has `format` / to_string which renders with colors based on terminal. We need to preserve exact formatting for all OTHER errors. We can: match e.kind() == ErrorKind::UnknownArgument, then take e.to_string() (or .render()), replace the "Usage: ..." line with alternation usage IF the error contains a tip (suggested arg). How to detect tip? e.to_string() contains "tip:" or e.get(ContextKind::SuggestedArg). Use clap::error::ContextKind / ContextValue.
# But use of try_get_matches changes behavior for --help: DisplayHelp error kind must be printed to stdout and exit 0 (e.print() does that? Error::print prints to stderr for errors and stdout for help? clap::Error::exit() handles: prints to stdout if kind is DisplayHelp/DisplayVersion else stderr, exits with 0/2. And *color*: when stderr is a tty, clap renders colored error (get_matches does that via Error::exit). We must replicate color behavior: reference in tty - do clap errors have color? Test reference in tmux with --invalid capture -e.

tmux new-session -d -s t -x 80 -y 24 './executable --invalid; echo EXIT:$?; sleep 3'
sleep 1; tmux capture-pane -t t -p -e | head -n 12
tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null; echo done"}

pub const WORDS: &str = include_str!("../data/words.txt");

fn split_lines(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    s.lines().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect()
}

pub enum Loaded {
    Ok(Vec<String>),
    FileNotFound,
}

pub fn load(n: &str, top: usize) -> Loaded {
    match n {
        "2" => Loaded::Ok(split_lines(BIGRAMS).into_iter().take(top).collect()),
        "3" => Loaded::Ok(split_lines(TRIGRAMS).into_iter().take(top).collect()),
        "4" => Loaded::Ok(split_lines(TETRAGRAMS).into_iter().take(top).collect()),
        "w" => Loaded::Ok(split_lines(WORDS).into_iter().take(top).collect()),
        _ => {
            let file = match File::open(n) {
                Ok(f) => f,
                Err(_) => return Loaded::FileNotFound,
            };
            let reader = BufReader::new(file);
            let mut tokens: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
            for line_from_bufread in reader.lines() {
                let line = line_from_bufread.unwrap();
                for tok in line.split(',') {
                    tokens.push(tok.to_string());
                }
            }
            Loaded::Ok(tokens.into_iter().take(top).collect())
        }
    }
}

// Keyboard layouts: three printable rows (top, home, bottom) plus a number
// row used by the emulation translation. The number-row entries are the
// unshifted characters of each layout; only azerty has letters there,
// the rest are digits/punctuation (which end up ignored when produced,
// because only alphabetic characters and space are accepted as input).

pub struct Layout {
    pub rows: [&'static str; 3],
    pub number_row: &'static str,
}

pub const QWERTY: Layout = Layout {
    rows: ["qwertyuiop[]", "asdfghjkl;'", "zxcvbnm,./"],
    number_row: "`1234567890-=",
};
pub const QWERTZ: Layout = Layout {
    rows: ["qwertzuiopü+", "asdfghjklöä", "yxcvbnm,.-"],
    number_row: "^1234567890ß´",
};
pub const AZERTY: Layout = Layout {
    rows: ["azertyuiop^$", "qsdfghjklmù", "wxcvbn,;:!"],
    // Unshifted AZERTY number row: ² & é " ' ( - è _ ç à ) =
    number_row: "²&é\"'(-è_çà)=",
};
pub const DVORAK: Layout = Layout {
    rows: ["',.pyfgcrl/=", "aoeuidhtns-", ";qjkxbmwvz"],
    number_row: "`1234567890[]",
};
pub const COLEMAK: Layout = Layout {
    rows: ["qwfpgjluy;[]", "arstdhneio'", "zxcvbkm,./"],
    number_row: "`1234567890-=",
};
pub const COLEMAKDH: Layout = Layout {
    rows: ["qwfpbjluy;[]", "arstgmneio'", "zxcdvkh,./"],
    number_row: "`1234567890-=",
};

pub fn parse_layout(name: &str) -> Layout {
    match name {
        "qwertz" => QWERTZ,
        "azerty" => AZERTY,
        "dvorak" => DVORAK,
        "colemak" => COLEMAK,
        "colemakdh" => COLEMAKDH,
        // "qwerty" and everything else falls back to qwerty
        _ => QWERTY,
    }
}

fn full_string(l: &Layout) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    s.push_str(l.number_row);
    for r in l.rows { s.push_str(r); }
    s
}

pub fn translate(c: char, emu_in: &str, emu_out: &str) -> char {
    // Per-row positional translation: number row, then the three rows.
    let lin = parse_layout(emu_in);
    let lout = parse_layout(emu_out);
    let in_rows: [&str; 4] = [lin.number_row, lin.rows[0], lin.rows[1], lin.rows[2]];
    let out_rows: [&str; 4] = [lout.number_row, lout.rows[0], lout.rows[1], lout.rows[2]];
    for (ri, row) in in_rows.iter().enumerate() {
        let chars: Vec<char> = row.chars().collect();
        if let Some(pos) = chars.iter().position(|&x| x == c) {
            let out_chars: Vec<char> = out_rows[ri].chars().collect();
            if pos < out_chars.len() {
                return out_chars[pos];
            } else {
                return c;
            }
        }
    }
    // Fall back to concatenated search (in case of length differences this
    // never triggers for the layouts above), otherwise pass through.
    let _ = full_string(&lin);
    c
}

fn run_loop(
    terminal: &mut Terminal<MyBackend<io::Stdout>>,
    game: &mut Game,
    kb_lines: &[String],
    ui_opts: &ui::UiOpts,
    has_emu: bool,
    emu_in: &str,
    emu_out: &str,
) -> io::Result<()> {
    let mut first = true;
    let start = Instant::now();
    loop {
        let mut cur_opts = ui_opts.clone();
        cur_opts.cat_frame = (start.elapsed().as_millis() / 160) as usize;
        terminal.draw(|f| {
            ui::draw(f, game, kb_lines, &cur_opts);
        })?;
        if first {
            first = false;
            game.next_lesson();
        }
        if event::poll(Duration::from_millis(16))? {
            if let Event::Key(key) = event::read()? {
                if key.kind != KeyEventKind::Press {
                    continue;
                }
                // Quit keys are not translated / counted
                if key.code == KeyCode::Esc {
                    break;
                }
                if key.modifiers == KeyModifiers::CONTROL && key.code == KeyCode::Char('c') {
                    break;
                }
                match key.code {
                    KeyCode::Char('h') if key.modifiers == KeyModifiers::CONTROL => {
                        // delete word: pop one trailing space, then the word
                        if game.input.last() == Some(&' ') {
                            game.pop_input_counted();
                        }
                        while let Some(&c) = game.input.last() {
                            if c == ' ' { break; }
                            game.pop_input_counted();
                        }
                        game.check_lesson_completed();
                    }
                    KeyCode::Backspace => {
                        game.pop_input_counted();
                        game.check_lesson_completed();
                    }
                    KeyCode::Enter => {
                        if game.input_byte_len() < game.cur_lesson.len() {
                            game.push_input(' ', true);
                        }
                        game.check_lesson_completed();
                    }
                    KeyCode::Char(mut c) => {
                        if has_emu {
                            c = layouts::translate(c, emu_in, emu_out);
                        }
                        if c.is_alphabetic() || c == ' ' {
                            let target: Vec<char> = game.cur_lesson.chars().collect();
                            if game.input_byte_len() < game.cur_lesson.len() {
                                if game.input.is_empty() {
                                    game.time_started = Instant::now();
                                }
                                game.total_keys += 1;
                                if target.get(game.input.len()) != Some(&c) {
                                    game.wrong += 1;
                                }
                                game.push_input(c, false);
                                game.check_lesson_completed();
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
